html:
A Māori Christian church and movement founded by the faith healer Tahupōtiki Wiremu Rātana, formally set up in 1925 at Rātana Pā near Whanganui, New Zealand. It was also a political movement.

Rātana had a vision in 1918, in the year of the great influenza, and began healing the sick. Thousands of Māori came to him, many disillusioned with the older churches and with land loss. His message joined Christian faith with a call for unity among all tribes, and the church's temple at Rātana Pā opened in 1928.

From the start the movement also worked for Māori rights under the Treaty of Waitangi. It formed an alliance with the Labour Party in 1936, and Rātana members won all four Māori seats in Parliament by 1943, holding them for decades. The alliance gave Māori a voice in the welfare reforms of the Labour years, such as the Social Security Act 1938. Its anniversary on 25 January still draws New Zealand's political leaders.
sum: A Māori Christian church and movement founded by the faith healer Tahupōtiki Wiremu Rātana, formally set up in 1925 at Rātana Pā near Whanganui, New Zealand. It was also a political movement.
